cues.text: Let's work through an archived pre-test revision question, Pre-test Question 2.
Here is the question.
A business needing to stream real-time click data from a website to downstream analytics tools would most appropriately deploy, blank.
So we must fill in that blank with the right technology.
Picture the scenario.
A website generates a constant flow of click events: every page view, every button press, every link followed.
The business wants that data to flow continuously, in real time, to downstream analytics tools.
So the key need is streaming events as they happen and delivering them onward.
There are four options.
Let me read each one.
Option one: AWS Glacier.
Option two: Google Cloud Spanner.
Option three: Apache Kafka for event streaming.
Option four: Apache Hive for ETL.
The archived LMS correct answer is option three: Apache Kafka for event streaming.
Now the source's reasoning for Question 2.
Kafka ingests and distributes event streams.
That is exactly what the scenario asks for: taking in a continuous flow of click events and passing it on to downstream consumers such as analytics tools.
Then the source explains why the other options do not fit.
AWS Glacier is archival storage.
It is meant for keeping data long term, not for moving a live stream of events.
Google Cloud Spanner is distributed SQL, which means it is a database for storing and querying relational data across many locations, not an event streaming platform.
And Apache Hive primarily supports analytics.
It is used to analyse data, rather than to ingest and distribute live click events as they arrive.
So the pattern to remember is this: when you see real-time event streams flowing from a source to downstream tools, think Apache Kafka.
When you see archival, think Glacier.
When you see distributed SQL, think Spanner.
And when you see analytics, think Hive.
